issues_confirmed: The spec permits over-watering by up to 2.2x. The 110-minute runtime was derived assuming exactly 3 irrigation events per week, 'spaced roughly every 2 to 3 days' (wiki/pages/first-runtime-rule-for-outdoor-tomato-drip-irrigation.md:26), but wiki/pages/first-recheck-rule-after-a-tomato-drip-irrigation-event.md:27-29 permits a full run the next day if the sensor has dried back to 25-30 cb. Using the page's own Penn State figure of 348 min of drip time per inch (first-runtime-rule-...:25), each 110-min event applies 0.316 in; 3 events/week = 0.95 in (on target), 7 events/week = 2.21 in against a 1 in/week target. No page in the repo caps event frequency or weekly volume.

No wiki page defines a minimum interval between irrigation events, so the TOO_SOON branch of the control function proposed in the last two TODO lists has no sourced constant and would have to invent one in code.
The two pages directly contradict each other on whether back-to-back daily runs are legal: first-runtime-rule-...:26 assumes 2-3 day spacing, first-recheck-rule-...:27-29 allows 1 day.
Repo contains zero executable code: 33 tracked files, 30 .md, 2 .json, 1 .pdf, no .py/.ino/.js/.ts of any kind (git ls-files).
